title: Supply vapes only as a pharmacist, under the therapeutic goods exceptions
what: Do not supply vaping goods unless an exception applies: for retail supply, the supplier must be a pharmacist (or an authorised medical or nurse practitioner) and the goods must be therapeutic goods entered on the Register or otherwise allowed.

sources.title: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
sources.quote: (1) A person commits an offence if the person supplies vaping goods in Australia. Penalty: Imprisonment for 7 years or 5,000 penalty units, or both.

sources.title: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
sources.quote: (10) This subsection applies in relation to the supply of the vaping goods by the person if: (a) the person is a pharmacist;

sources.title: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
sources.quote: (4) If the applicant gives the Secretary the certificate referred to in subparagraph (3)(c)(i) or the notice referred to in subparagraph (3)(c)(ii), the Secretary must: (a) include the goods in the Register;

reach.condition: if it would supply vaping goods
reach.note: Pharmacies may supply within the exceptions; other retailers may not supply at all.

sources.title: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
sources.quote: (1) A person commits an offence if the person supplies vaping goods in Australia. Penalty: Imprisonment for 7 years or 5,000 penalty units, or both.

confidence_note: The Act's own words make supplying vaping goods an offence unless an exception applies.

assessment.summary: Vapes may be sold only by pharmacies for therapeutic use, after bans on imports of disposable and non-therapeutic vapes. It closes other legal retail channels and may push supply to illicit sellers.

marks.reason: Restricts lawful supply to pharmacies, closing the market to other retailers.

assessment.confidence_note: Public health benefits, the reason for the policy, are not weighed here. Marks copied from the register item cth-vaping-reforms-2024 so the two agree.
